root_cause_hint: rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs, fn handle_foreach_command (lines 1753-1771): only calls `self.define_vars_from_list(&args[0], *tok, scope_path)` for the FIRST varList token, then jumps straight to `args.last()` / `arg_tokens.last()` as the body — args[2], args[4], ... (any further varList/list pairs in the `foreach varList1 list1 ?varList2 list2 ...? body` form) are never passed to define_vars_from_list, so their names are never registered as local variables at all. This is despite the command's own registry spec at rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/foreach_.rs explicitly documenting and arity-validating exactly this multi-pair form (`arity: Arity::stepped(3, Arity::UNLIMITED, 2)`, comment: "confirmed against tclsh 8.6.14"). Fix: loop `for i in (0..args.len()-1).step_by(2)` binding each `args[i]` varList (mirroring the arity spec's own stride of 2), keeping only the last arg as body. Downstream, the wrong-location symptom on the real corpus is explained by rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/definition.rs::lookup_var_in_scope_chain (shared by hover.rs and go-to-definition): since `foreach`/`if`/etc. don't introduce new analyser scopes (correctly modelling Tcl's lack of block scoping), all top-level code shares one flat global Scope whose `variables` map is looked up by bare name only; with no VarDef ever created for the skipped varList, a `$name` reference falls through to whatever other same-named VarDef happens to exist anywhere in that flat scope — in pixdoc.tcl, the coincidental unrelated `foreach name {...}` at line 447.

summary: Go-to-definition correctly resolves the real pattern (`source [file join [file dirname [info script]] data_b64.test]`, isEqual/getbase64 called bare afterward) via the existing M9 stage-9.2 computed-path folder plus an on-disk read_document fallback — that part is REFUTED as a bug, it works. But textDocument/references is genuinely broken for any symbol reached this way: querying references from a call site of a source'd-in proc returns ONLY the proc's declaration and silently drops every call site in the SAME document you're querying from — including the exact call site the cursor sits on. Root cause: the single-document reference provider requires a local declaration to anchor on (none exists — the proc lives in the sourced file), and the cross-document provider explicitly excludes the calling document, wrongly assuming the local pass already covers it. A second, independent bug compounds this in the real corpus: `.test` (the file extension used by all 5 real sibling test_*.test files, standard tcltest convention) is missing from the LSP's workspace-scan extension allow-list, so sibling files that also call the shared helper are invisible unless a client happens to open them too.

Net effect: `PackageResolver::provides(name)` (~L720-723) is false for any load-only package whose directory has no other .tcl file. Consumer: rust/tcl-lsp-server/src/lib.rs `refine_w120_diagnostics` (~L11376-11405) computes `unknowable = package_requires.iter().any(|p| p != "Tcl" && !registry.provides_package(p) && !resolver.provides(p))` and, if true, strips every W120 from the document — conflating "we can't enumerate this package's commands" with "we've never heard of this package at all". The repo's own test `build_package_resolver_picks_up_a_discovered_installation_package` (rust/tcl-lsp-server/src/lib.rs ~L12899-12923) already had to add a synthetic marker .tcl file to its Tk pkgIndex.tcl fixture to dodge this exact gap ("The package has no source file (a C extension loaded via `load`); the fallback lists the dir's *.tcl — none here, so give it a marker .tcl."), but no test covers the realistic zero-companion-file case (pix's actual layout). A minimal 5-file analogue (namespace `mypkg` with `version`/`_intro` declared in mypkg.tcl, three sibling files each opening a `mypkg::modX` child namespace, loaded via pkgIndex.tcl/`package require` exactly like the real project) reproduces the same single-file-works/cross-file-fails split, and a plain-`source` 2-file variant (no package machinery at all) reproduces it too, so it isn't about package-loading indirection — it's that the variable-definition lookup never looks outside the current document. By contrast, a fully-qualified cross-file CLASS reference (`mypkg::moda::Widget` defined in one file, instantiated in another via plain `source`) resolves correctly, and the real corpus's own `WorkspaceClass`/`WorkspaceProc` machinery clearly supports cross-file proc/class navigation — so this is specifically a namespace-*variable* gap, not a general "cross-file resolution is broken" issue. Separately (same investigation, same file, not the primary claim here): the literal `::tomato` argument of `[namespace children ::tomato]` — the exact token the mined note centers on — never resolves via go-to-definition/hover/references either, but this reproduces even in a single file with a single trivial `namespace eval mypkg { ... }` reopening, so it is a broader, pre-existing gap (no namespace-name-as-argument wiring at all for `namespace children`/likely its `exists`/`delete`/`parent`/`qualifiers`/`tail` siblings, unlike `namespace eval` whose own name argument IS tagged `ArgRole::Name`) rather than something specific to unioning many files.

summary: The assigned finding's exact hypothesis (LSP guesses wrong among IntersectionWithPlane/Ray/Line based on `switch -glob [$obj GetType]`) is REFUTED: the LSP correctly abstains (no location, no hover) on that literal `[$obj GetType]` call, both in a faithful two-block repro and directly against the real Plane.tcl -- sound behaviour for a genuinely dynamic dispatch, and the 3 literal `tomato::mathplane::IntersectionWith{Plane,Ray,Line}` calls resolve/reference correctly (unambiguous qualified names). BUT tracing *why* it abstains uncovered a distinct, root-caused, CONFIRMED bug in the exact same class: `oo::define ClassName {...}` extending a class already created via `oo::class create ClassName {...}` (the idiom all 9 of tomato's classes use -- constructor in `create`, every method incl. GetType/IntersectionWith in a later `define`) never extends the class's recorded body_span to cover that oo::define block. Every feature that gates on "is the cursor lexically inside this class" then silently fails inside it: go-to-definition/hover on a plain, single-target `my Method` internal call return nothing, and hover/references on a method's own declaration there return nothing too -- verified on real, unmodified Plane.tcl (`my Normal` in RootPoint) and Ray3d.tcl (`my ThroughPoint` in ShortestLineTo), and reproduced from scratch. This is a false negative (misses a 100% statically-resolvable answer), not a wrong-location bug, but it is pervasive: it silently disables go-to-def/hover/references for the majority of method bodies in any TclOO codebase using this extremely common two-statement class-definition convention.

Identical failure on Plane.tcl's `my Normal` inside `RootPoint` (0-based line 294 col 21, target `method Normal {}` at 0-based line 111 col 11): definition -> 0 locations, hover -> none. Positive control on the SAME real file/session: a plain same-file literal proc call, `tomato::mathplane::IntersectionWithPlane` at Plane.tcl line 133 col 43 -> `definition` correctly returns its `proc` at line 422 col 5-45 -- proving the file/session loads fine and the defect is specific to the class-body_span containment gate, not a general breakdown. Minimal from-scratch isolation (twoblock/plane_tb.tcl): `oo::class create geo::Plane {constructor{args}{}}` then separately `oo::define geo::Plane { method GetType{}{...} method IntersectionWith{obj}{switch -glob [$obj GetType] {...}} method WhichAmI{}{return [my GetType]} export ... }` -- `definition plane_tb.tcl 43 19` (on `my GetType`) -> 0 locations; `hover` -> none; `references` from GetType's own decl (line 18 col 11) -> 0 locations (not even itself). Control: the SAME logic combined into a SINGLE `oo::class create geo::Plane { method GetType{} ... method IntersectionWith{...} export ... }` block (audit/76/plane.tcl) resolves fine -- `hover` on `$p1 GetType` (known class) -> "**method** `::geo::Plane::GetType`", and `references` from GetType's decl finds both itself and the call -- isolating the trigger precisely to the two-block create-then-define reopen shape. tclsh9.0 on all repros confirms the runtime ground truth (plane-plane/plane-ray/plane-line dispatch by $obj's actual class, and `$p1 GetType` == ::geo::Plane), matching the note's premise that the switch's target genuinely varies by runtime class.
root_cause_hint: rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs, `handle_oo_define_command` (~line 2810-2949, specifically ~2866-2898): `let mut class_def = self.result.all_classes.remove(&qualified).unwrap_or_else(|| { ...stub with body_span = whole-oo::define-span... });` -- when the class WAS already known (the common case: an earlier `oo::class create` in the same/merged analysis), it reuses that existing ClassDef's `body_span` (set narrowly by `handle_oo_class_command` ~line 2752-2758 to just the `oo::class create` call's own body/name span) verbatim and never unions it with this `oo::define` invocation's span, even though `parse_oo_definition_body` (called right after) is about to populate most of the class's methods from it. Telling contrast: the `unwrap_or_else` STUB branch (taken only when the class is genuinely unseen, e.g. true cross-file) DOES compute `body_span = Span::new(name_span.start(), last_token.span.end())` covering the whole oo::define call -- the comment at ~2877-2884 even explains this is required so members "stay nested inside" the class's span -- confirming the fix is understood in one branch but missing in the other. Downstream consumers that gate on `cursor_offset` falling inside `class_def.body_span` then silently miss: rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/definition.rs `enclosing_class_at` (~line 438-445, feeds the `inst == "my"` branch of `instance_method_definition` ~line 272-278) and `lookup_class_member` (~line 313-355, the bare-word class-member fallback); and rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/references.rs `find_class_member_references` (~line 844-858, same containment pattern, gates `class_member_references`). Fix direction: when merging an `oo::define` into an existing `ClassDef`, extend `class_def.body_span` to the union of its old span and this invocation's span (mirroring the stub branch's span computation) rather than leaving it untouched.

summary: Vector3d.tcl's `method * {type}` (lines 296-317, real file) reads `$other` in its isa-object branch even though the method's only parameter is `type` (`other` belongs to the sibling `+`/`-`/`==`/`!=` methods). This is a genuine, verified runtime bug: tclsh8.6 and tclsh9.0.4 both crash with `can't read "other": no such variable` the moment `*` is invoked with an object operand. The LSP's diagnostics pass produces 0 findings on this file (and 0 findings on a minimal, structurally-identical, unconditional analogue), while the exact same unbound-variable shape inside a plain `proc` correctly fires W210 twice. Root cause isolated in source: TclOO method bodies are fully compiled to CFG/SSA `FunctionUnit`s (`compilation_unit.rs::build_method_units`) but the per-function diagnostic driver in `diagnostics.rs` only iterates `cu.procedures`, never `cu.methods`, so the entire `emit_cfg_ssa_diagnostics_for_function_full` family (W210 read-before-set, W211 unused-var, W220 dead-store, divide-by-zero, interval-bounds, unused-param, etc.) silently never runs on any TclOO (or snit) method body. This is a systemic false-negative gap, not just a one-off miss on this pattern.

Within a single file the LSP handles this correctly (definition/references resolve Pi()/Inv() to ::tcl::mathfunc::Pi/Inv and correctly ignore a same-file decoy proc tomato::helper::Pi). But across files — the actual dominant real-world shape in this corpus — the LSP's own goto-definition/find-references correctly resolve Pi()/Inv() cross-file to the ::tcl::mathfunc definitions in the sibling file, while the diagnostics pass (W123 'unknown command') does NOT consult that same cross-file knowledge and fires a false 'Unknown command' HINT on the identical call sites, plus offers a quickfix that would replace 'Pi' with 'ni' (a real but unrelated Tcl operator) if accepted — i.e. two subsystems in the same server disagree about whether the exact same statically-resolvable symbol exists, and one of them proposes an edit that would break working code. root_cause_hint: Correct path (definition/references, not buggy): rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/commands.rs `record_expr_function_invocations` (~line 2006) records each `NAME(args)` in an expr as an invocation resolved to `::tcl::mathfunc::NAME`; downstream qualified-name resolution correctly distinguishes it from an ordinary same-tail proc in another namespace. Buggy path: rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/unresolved.rs `w123_invocation_resolves` (~lines 336-432) / `emit_w123_for_invocations` (~line 437) validate every invocation's bare `name` only against the ordinary command registry (`registry_names`, built from `tcl_registry::CommandRegistry` filtered by dialect profile) plus workspace proc/class/alias/ensemble tail names (`build_w123_known_names`, ~line 153) — it never checks `inv.resolved_qualified_name` for a `::tcl::mathfunc::` prefix nor consults `tcl_syntax::expr::mathfunc::added_in` (rust/tcl-syntax/src/expr/mathfunc.rs:128), the crate's own canonical, version-gated list of real `expr` math functions that a sibling diagnostic already uses for the same invocations: `emit_expr_function_dialect_diagnostics` in rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/validity.rs (~line 3082, W002 "disabled in dialect"). `acos`/`sqrt`/`max`/etc. correctly aren't in `registry_names` (they are not callable as ordinary top-level commands — confirmed `tclsh9.0 -c 'acos -1'` -> "invalid command name"), so they fall through to the false W123. `Pi()` only escapes it by accident: `proc_tail_names` is built namespace-blind from every proc's bare tail, so the corpus's own `proc tcl::mathfunc::Pi {}` (or even the decoy `ns::helper::Pi`) happens to suppress the diagnostic for the literal string "Pi" regardless of which one actually resolves. Likely fix: in `w123_invocation_resolves`, thread `inv.resolved_qualified_name` through and add a branch that treats a `::tcl::mathfunc::<name>` resolution as known when `tcl_syntax::expr::mathfunc::added_in(name)` is `Some` (mirroring validity.rs's usage), rather than relying solely on the coincidental proc-tail set.

No bug found.

A developer using "go to definition" on `tk fontchooser show`-style calls (or renaming/auditing usages of the implementation proc) gets nothing, silently, with no diagnostic explaining why.
root_cause_hint: rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs:1611, in `Analyser::handle_namespace_ensemble` -- `let ns = self.namespace_from_scope_path(scope_path);` uses the lexical-only namespace resolver (rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/scope.rs:554), which is explicitly documented and unit-tested (scope.rs:1267 `namespace_from_scope_path_skips_proc_scopes`) to skip `Proc` scopes and only accumulate lexically-enclosing `namespace eval` blocks. When `namespace ensemble create` (no `-command`) runs inside a proc whose own namespace comes only from its qualified name (no enclosing `namespace eval`), this returns `"::"` instead of the proc's real defining namespace, so `ensemble_key` (used to file `AnalysisResult::ensemble_subcommand_targets` at handlers.rs:1630-1637) and `ensemble_namespaces` both get mis-keyed under `"::"`. The lookup at call sites (`record_ensemble_subcommand_invocation`, rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/commands.rs:1468: `self.result.ensemble_subcommand_targets.get(resolved_cmd)`) uses the *correctly*-resolved `resolved_cmd` (e.g. `::app::widget`), which never matches the `"::"`-filed entry, so the probe reference is silently never recorded. The fix is to use `self.command_resolution_namespace(scope_path)` (scope.rs:601) instead, exactly as `Analyser::handle_proc_command` already does for the analogous "proc defined by qualified name, no enclosing namespace eval" case (handlers.rs:677-682, whose own doc comment describes this exact failure mode almost verbatim). No existing unit test for `handle_namespace_ensemble` (handlers.rs ~4895-5065) or the full-pipeline `namespace_ensemble_map_and_subcommands_record_command_references` test (handlers.rs ~4986) exercises this shape -- all of them construct the ensemble's enclosing scope as a literal `Scope::new(ScopeKind::Namespace, ...)` pushed directly, or wrap the `create` call lexically inside `namespace eval`, so the qualified-name-outside-namespace-eval case (the actual fontchooser.tcl shape) has no coverage.

summary: The Tk-specific diagnostics TK1001 (pack/grid geometry-manager conflict) and TK1002 (widget references non-existent parent) use analyser state (`tk_created_widgets`, `tk_geometry`) that is a single flat, un-namespaced HashSet/BTreeMap shared across the whole file walk. The general `interp create NAME; NAME eval {...}` isolation machinery (`isolate_interp_eval_body`) already opens a separate scope for procs/vars/safe-interp state when walking a child interpreter's eval body, but never saves/restores or keys the Tk widget-path tracking by interpreter domain. Since dialog1.tcl's own pattern (`interp create child; load {} Tk child; child eval { ...creates '.', '.t'... }`) gives the child interpreter a completely separate Tk window hierarchy, a same-named widget path used both inside the child eval body and in the parent script gets conflated by the LSP as if it were the same widget, producing both a false-positive TK1001 and a false-negative TK1002.
failure_scenario:
Repro A (false positive TK1001) at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-tcl-lsp/b4c77bf3-47fd-5ba4-822a-000fa233bcc1/scratchpad/audit/91/dialog1_repro_tk1001.tcl:
  package require Tk
  interp create child
  load {} Tk child
  child eval { frame .top; pack .top.a }
  frame .top
  grid .top.b
Real semantics: `child`'s `.top` (created inside the isolated child-eval body) and the parent's own later `frame .top` are two unrelated windows in two separate Tk hierarchies (proven generally by oracle_interp_isolation.tcl: a command/proc defined inside `child eval {...}` never appears in the parent's `info commands`, and vice versa -- this is the exact mechanism Tk widget-creation commands rely on to register their path as a command). So `pack .top.a` (in the child) and `grid .top.b` (in the parent) are not a real geometry-manager conflict and the script would run fine. The LSP instead reports:
  WARNING TK1001 19:9-19:15 Geometry manager conflict: cannot mix 'pack' and 'grid' in the same parent '.top'.
  WARNING TK1001 23:5-23:11 Geometry manager conflict: cannot mix 'pack' and 'grid' in the same parent '.top'.
(deterministic across repeated runs; a same-shape single-interpreter control file with a REAL conflict, control_tk1001_conflict.tcl, correctly fires TK1001 too, confirming the checker mechanism itself works -- only the interp-crossing case is wrong.)

Repro B (false negative TK1002) at .../audit/91/dialog1_repro_tk1002.tcl:
  package require Tk
  interp create child
  load {} Tk child
  child eval { frame .top; frame .top.inner }
  frame .top.other
Real semantics: the parent interpreter's own Tk hierarchy never creates `.top` (only the child's separate hierarchy did), so `frame .top.other` in the parent would raise `bad window path name ".top"` at run time. The LSP reports 0 diagnostics for this file, silently missing the error. A same-shape single-interpreter control (control_tk1002_missing_parent.tcl: `package require Tk; frame .top.other` with no prior `.top` anywhere) correctly fires TK1002, confirming the checker itself is sound -- only the interp-crossing case suppresses it (because `.top` was already inserted into the shared `tk_created_widgets` set while walking the child's isolated body).
root_cause_hint: rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/state.rs:214 and :218 (`tk_created_widgets: HashSet<String>`, `tk_geometry: BTreeMap<String, TkGeometryUsage>` -- single flat fields on `Analyser`, never keyed by interpreter domain) read/written from rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/tk_checks.rs:147-194 (`emit_tk_checks`) and flushed in tk_checks.rs:282-314 (`flush_tk_geometry_diagnostics`). The isolation boundary that should scope them already exists for every other kind of analyser state (procs, vars, safe-interp hidden/exposed sets) in rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs:1176-1240 (`isolate_interp_eval_body`, called from both the literal `interp eval PATH {...}` handler at handlers.rs:1106 and the `NAME eval {...}` handle-form handler at handlers.rs:1278 `handle_interp_handle_eval_command` -- exactly the `child eval {...}` spelling used in dialog1.tcl) -- it pushes/pops `self.interp_path_stack` and `self.safe_interp_stack` around the child body walk but has no equivalent push/pop (or domain-keying) for `tk_created_widgets`/`tk_geometry`, so `emit_tk_checks` (dispatched per-command from commands.rs:960 inside `emit_dispatch_site_diagnostics`, which runs unconditionally for every command including ones inside an isolated child body) sees and pollutes the same global sets regardless of which interpreter's widget hierarchy a given `frame`/`pack`/`grid` call actually belongs to.

summary: find-references (and the shared `command_invocations` substrate that also feeds rename/call-hierarchy/code-lens) silently drops every call site of a proc that is used as a trace/callback handler via the idiomatic `[namespace code [list ProcName ...]]` wrapper — the exact pattern Tk's own library/fontchooser.tcl uses 10 times (lines 294-303, 324-328) for its `Tracer` callback — even though go-to-definition and hover resolve the identical token at the identical position correctly, and tclsh proves the callback deterministically resolves to that proc with no runtime/dynamic data involved.
failure_scenario: Repro mirrors fontchooser.tcl's Setup/Tracer/Done: `proc ::demo::Tracer {var1 var2 op} {...}`; `proc ::demo::Setup {} { trace add variable [namespace which -variable S](size) write [namespace code [list Tracer]] }`; `proc ::demo::Done {} { trace remove variable S(size) write [namespace code [list Tracer]] }`. Oracle (tclsh9.0 and tclsh8.6, identical): `trace info variable ::demo::S(size)` after Setup returns `{write {::namespace inscope ::demo Tracer}}`, and `set ::demo::S(size) 42` actually fires it (prints `TRACED: ::demo::S(size) write -> 42`) — proving `Tracer` inside `[list Tracer]` is a real, statically-determined reference to proc `::demo::Tracer` (namespace baked in from the enclosing proc's own namespace, no runtime data anywhere). LSP: `definition repro.tcl 33 36` (cursor on `Tracer` at the trace-add call site) and `definition repro.tcl 38 62` (trace-remove site) both correctly jump to `repro.tcl 26:5-26:19` (the proc decl), and `hover` at the same coordinates shows the correct `proc ::demo::Tracer {var1 var2 op}` signature — so the LSP's own resolver knows the right answer at that exact token. But `references repro.tcl 26 13` (cursor on the `Tracer` declaration) returns only 1 location — the declaration itself — 0 of the 2 real call sites. Re-running `references` with the cursor placed directly on `Tracer` at either call site (33:36 or 38:62) returns the same single location, not even including the very call site the cursor sits on. root_cause_hint: rust/tcl-compiler/src/signature_scan/command_prefix.rs::extract_prefix_head only recognises a literal bareword head (TokenType::Esc) or a braced-list head (TokenType::Str); a `[...]`-headed command-prefix argument (TokenType::Cmd — exactly what `[namespace code [list Tracer]]` is, sitting in trace's arg-index-3 `commandPrefix` position registered via trace_add_command_prefixes/trace_remove_command_prefixes in rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/trace.rs) falls through to None, so record_command_prefix_invocations (rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/commands.rs:1278, whose own doc comment says "a dynamic $cb / [..] head stays unrecorded") contributes nothing to command_invocations. namespace code's own registry spec (rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/namespace_.rs, `code` subcommand) marks its sole arg ArgRole::Body, dispatched via dispatch_body_arguments -> Analyser::analyse_body (rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/commands.rs:128), which immediately returns when body_tok.kind != TokenType::Str — a no-op for the Cmd-kind `[list Tracer]` argument too. The generic nested-substitution scan (record_invocations_from_cmd_token, commands.rs:1573) does descend into `[namespace code [list Tracer]]` but only records the builtin heads it finds (`namespace`, `list`), with no notion that list's own literal argument names a command in this context. Compare the already-implemented, narrowly-scoped precedent for the sibling idiom `namespace eval $ns [list namespace unknown $handler]`: Analyser::detect_list_wrapped_namespace_unknown (commands.rs:1629, added for issue #923 idx 110) — no analogous one-level unwrap exists yet for `namespace code [list ProcName ...]`. references()/proc_references (rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/references.rs:393) and proc_reference_spans (references.rs:89) read only analysis.command_invocations, so the missing entry silently drops these call sites; definition()/hover instead succeed via an unrelated, context-blind "any bareword under the cursor is a potential proc reference" fallback (rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/definition.rs:193-218, resolve_called_proc) that never consults command_invocations at all — hence the definition-vs-references asymmetry observed.

So the LSP only gives up on the real pattern because `$method`'s value is knowable solely from TraceOption's *callers* (megawidget.tcl:255,288) -- genuine interprocedural parameter-constant-propagation across two separate method bodies, not "one hop of namespace/mixin/ensemble simulation." summary: tearoff.tcl's two indirection mechanics were both reproduced faithfully; the -tearoffcommand/cget/uplevel round trip (TearOffMenu) is handled correctly (abstains where it must, resolves where it can), but MenuDup's `set cmd [list menu $dst -type $type]; ...; eval $cmd` shape exposes a real bug: the LSP's indirect-dispatch tracker only fires when a $var sits at a command's HEAD position, never when that variable is passed as eval/uplevel's ARGUMENT. root_cause_hint: rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs, fn handle_oo_class_command (starts line 2941). The is_class_definer guard (lines 2968-2976) is: `self.registry.as_ref().and_then(|r| r.get(cmd_name)).is_some_and(|s| s.traits.contains(IS_OO_METACLASS) && s.definition_body.is_some_and(|g| g.family == TclOo))`. This can only ever match the 4 built-in metaclass commands already in tcl-registry (oo::class, oo::configurable, oo::abstract, oo::singleton) — it looks cmd_name up in the static registry only, never in `self.result.all_classes` (where ::tk::Megawidget's own ClassDef, including its literal `superclass: ::oo::class`, is already correctly recorded — see symbols output `Class Megawidget : ::oo::class`). So a locally-defined class that is itself a metaclass (superclass chain reaches ::oo::class, with or without a `self method create` override) never satisfies is_class_definer, and `Megawidget create Name ...` falls through as an unrecognized command — Name never enters all_classes. Extending the guard to also accept "cmd_name resolves to an already-recorded ClassDef whose (transitive) superclass chain includes ::oo::class" would fix at least the shallow case (recognizing SimpleWidget/FocusableWidget as classes using the literal, explicitly-passed superclasses argument) without needing to simulate self method create's body contents at all; correctly inferring the *implicit* spliced ::tk::MegawidgetClass superclass would need one further, harder step (reading the self-method-create body's `next`-argument template).

root_cause_hint: rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs::handle_oo_class_command (~lines 2941-2984): only treats `cmd_name create/new/createWithNamespace ...` as a class-creating call when `self.registry.get(cmd_name)` carries `tcl_registry::Traits::IS_OO_METACLASS`. That trait is a fixed property of exactly 5 registry-builtin specs — rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/oo_class.rs, oo_abstract.rs, oo_configurable.rs, oo_object.rs, oo_singleton.rs — and is never derived/propagated for a workspace-defined class whose own `superclass` chain includes `oo::class` (i.e. a user-defined metaclass such as Tk's own `::tk::Megawidget`, created via a perfectly ordinary, already-recognized `oo::class create Megawidget {superclass ::oo::class ...}`). Because `Megawidget` has no registry spec at all, `is_class_definer` is false and the function returns early, so `SimpleWidget`/`FocusableWidget`/`IconList` never enter `result.all_classes`. The downstream MRO walker that resolves `next` (rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/class_hierarchy.rs::next_provider, confirmed correct by the control repro) is never even reached for them since it has nothing in `all_classes` to walk. Note a complete fix needs two parts: (1) propagate metaclass-ness transitively — a class is itself a valid class-creator if its own (possibly indirect) superclasses include `oo::class`/another metaclass, not just registry-listed names; (2) generalize the fixed body-argument indexing (`oo_class_arg_roles` in oo_class.rs:45-56, and the `args.get(2)` assumption in `handle_oo_class_command`) which hardcodes the builtin `create Name body` / `new body` / `createWithNamespace Name ns body` shapes and would mis-index the body for `Megawidget create Name Superclasses Body` (body is args[3], not args[2]) even if part (1) were fixed.

root_cause_hint: rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/commands.rs::Analyser::analyse_body (~line 129): `if body_tok.kind != TokenType::Str { return; }` skips all per-command processing — including `record_arg_var_reads` (line ~244, the mechanism that populates VarDef.references consumed by hover/definition/references) — whenever a body is a `[...]` command-substitution rather than a literal `{...}` block. rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs::Analyser::handle_namespace_eval_command (~line 1099-1167) is the caller for `namespace eval NS BODY`: for `BODY = [list source [file join $NS_VAR $PARAM.tcl]]` it still creates the child namespace scope (visible via `symbols`, e.g. "Namespace :: (line 29)"), but the `analyse_body` call on that body is a no-op per the gate above, so nested `$var` reads are never captured into the enclosing proc's scope chain — even though the separate nested-substitution walker used for bareword command-name recognition (`run_nested_command_diagnostics`/`collect_substitution_heads` in analyser/commands.rs, documented as descending into any `[...]` region "invisible to the main walk") does reach the same region, which is why "source"/"file" still hover correctly there. This mirrors the already-fixed idx=110 gap (`detect_list_wrapped_namespace_unknown`, same file) which added a narrow command-shape detector for `[list namespace unknown ...]` but not a general variable-reference recorder for list-wrapped/dynamic body arguments of namespace eval (or uplevel/eval/after, likely similarly affected). The secondary hover-misattribution bug is most likely in rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/hover.rs's word/position classification (pub fn hover_with_profile, ~line 193 onward) for a parameter-list declaration token that happens to also be a registry command name — it resolves the registry command before/instead of recognizing the position as inside a `{param ...}` declaration list.

summary: demos/ttkscale.tcl:34 calls `tcl::mathfunc::int $idx` as an ordinary fully-qualified plain command (not `expr{int(...)}`). That literal call is handled fine by the LSP (int is always available, so no diagnostic is expected and none fires; go-to-def correctly abstains since int is a C builtin with no Tcl source). But probing the general mechanism the note describes ("resolver tuned only for mathfunc-in-expr misses the plain-command spelling") with a version-gated sibling function (`isinf`, Tcl 9.0+) exposes a real, confirmed bug: `rust/tcl-registry` has ZERO CommandSpec entries for `tcl::mathfunc::*` (unlike its sibling `tcl::mathop::*`, which is fully registered under all three spellings in mathop_generated.rs). Consequence: `set r [tcl::mathfunc::isinf 1.0]`, opened under the server's default tcl8.6 dialect, gets 0 diagnostics — even though tclsh8.6 proves this call unconditionally raises `invalid command name "tcl::mathfunc::isinf"` (isinf is 9.0+ only). The identical function called as `expr {isinf(1.0)}` correctly gets `WARNING W002 '::tcl::mathfunc::isinf' is disabled in the active dialect profile ('tcl8.6')`, because that path is checked by a separate, expr-only mechanism (`emit_expr_function_dialect_diagnostics`) that the plain-command dispatch path never reaches. Separately (and REFUTED as a concern): go-to-definition/find-references on the plain-command spelling of a *user-defined* `::tcl::mathfunc::NAME` proc work correctly (verified with a `double2` proc), so the general qualified-command resolution machinery itself is fine — the gap is specifically registry data + the dialect-gating diagnostic pathway. Note: a related but distinct mathfunc bug (bare/unqualified calls to a `tcl::mathfunc`-namespaced proc being wrongly treated as resolvable) is already tracked separately as idx=30 in this same audit; this finding does not duplicate it.

root_cause_hint: Missing registry data, not missing logic: `rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/` has mathop.rs + mathop_generated.rs registering every `tcl::mathop::*` operator under all 3 spellings (bare, `tcl::mathop::+`, `::tcl::mathop::+`), but there is no equivalent mathfunc.rs/mathfunc_generated.rs — zero CommandSpec entries anywhere for `tcl::mathfunc::*` (grep -rn mathfunc rust/tcl-registry -> no matches). Effects: (1) rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/validity.rs:539 `emit_w002_disabled_command` — the generic, already-correctly-wired per-dispatch-site W002 check (confirmed working for other qualified names like tcltest::bytestring) — finds `registry.known_in_any_dialect("tcl::mathfunc::isinf")` false, treats it as wholly unknown, and defers to W123. (2) rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/unresolved.rs:379 `w123_invocation_resolves` unconditionally treats any name containing "::" as resolved ("conservative skip"), so W123 never picks it up either -> total silence. (3) The one place that *does* know the real version-gating fact, `emit_expr_function_dialect_diagnostics` (validity.rs:3082), reads `tcl_syntax::expr::mathfunc::added_in` (rust/tcl-syntax/src/expr/mathfunc.rs:128) but is only invoked via `expr_function_calls`/`record_expr_function_invocations` (rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/commands.rs:2022-2068), which is fed exclusively from text recognized as an actual `expr{...}` string — never from the ordinary bracket-command-substitution dispatch path (`push_collected_heads`, commands.rs:2075) that handles `[tcl::mathfunc::isinf 1.0]`. Fix direction: add mathfunc_generated.rs entries named `tcl::mathfunc::<name>` / `::tcl::mathfunc::<name>` (NOT bare `<name>` — unlike mathop operators, bare mathfunc names are not real commands) with `dialects` sourced from the same `tcl_syntax::expr::mathfunc::added_in` table, so `emit_w002_disabled_command` picks them up for free via its existing registry-driven logic.

summary: Hover/go-to-definition/find-references conflate a proc parameter's own bare declaration-name and default-value tokens with an unrelated command/proc of the same name, because only `$`-prefixed tokens are recognized as variables before falling through to generic bareword command resolution.
failure_scenario:
Real code: library/tk.tcl:202 `proc ::tk::RestoreFocusGrab {grab focus {destroy destroy}} { ... if {$destroy eq "withdraw"} {...} else { destroy $grab } }`. tclsh9.0/8.6 both prove: `$destroy` always reads the local parameter; bare `destroy $grab` always calls the (possibly-shadowing) command — separate namespaces, no ambiguity, no dynamism.

On the UNMODIFIED corpus slice (lines 1-230 of tk.tcl, `info complete`-verified), cwd = .../audit/104/real_slice:
- `hover tk_slice.tcl 201 41` (cursor on the parameter-name `destroy` inside `{destroy destroy}`) returns the Tk builtin's doc: "**`destroy`** — built-in command ... Requires: `package require Tk`" — wrong; should describe the 3rd parameter of `::tk::RestoreFocusGrab`.
- `hover tk_slice.tcl 201 49` (cursor on the default-value literal `destroy`, a plain string) returns the SAME wrong builtin doc — this token is pure data, not a reference to anything.
- Control (correct): `hover tk_slice.tcl 213 6` (the real `$destroy` use) correctly returns "**Variable** `destroy` — 1 reference(s)"; `hover tk_slice.tcl 216 5` (the real `destroy $grab` call) correctly returns the builtin doc.

On a self-contained, tclsh-verified minimal repro (audit/104/repro.tcl) that adds an explicit global `proc destroy {w} {...}` to make the shadowing concrete and runnable:
- `definition repro.tcl 22 35` (cursor exactly on the parameter's own name token) returns `repro.tcl 18:5-18:12` — the UNRELATED global proc's declaration, not "already at the parameter decl" / the parameter's own binding.
- `definition repro.tcl 22 43` (cursor on the default-value literal) returns the same wrong location.
- `references repro.tcl 22 35` returns `[18:5-18:12, 27:8-27:15]` (the unrelated proc's decl + its call site) and OMITS the parameter's real usages (`$destroy` at 23:26 and 24:9) entirely.
- Control (correct): `definition repro.tcl 24 9` (the real `$destroy` use) correctly returns `22:35-22:42` (the parameter decl); `references repro.tcl 24 9` correctly returns exactly the 3 real variable sites.

Since rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/rename.rs's `rename`/`prepare_rename` are built directly on `crate::references::*`, invoking rename on the parameter's declaration token in a workspace containing a same-named proc/command would very likely rename the wrong symbol while leaving the actual parameter and its `$destroy` usages untouched (inferred from the references bug above, not directly executed — the CLI harness exposes no `rename` subcommand).
root_cause_hint: rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/hover.rs::find_var_at_position (~line 2183) only recognizes a literal `$`/`${...}` prefix as "this position is a variable". A proc's own parameter-name and default-value tokens (bare text inside `{name default}`) never match, so they fall through in three separate providers to generic bareword lookup with no check for "cursor is inside an enclosing proc's own parameter-list span": rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/hover.rs::hover_with_profile (falls through past the `find_var_at_position` gate at ~line 229 to `proc_hover_at`/`builtin_command_hover_text` around lines 194-208 and ~360-369); rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/definition.rs::definition (lines 141-286, specifically the "Otherwise it is a CALL" `resolve_called_proc` fallback at ~line 233); rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/references.rs::references (lines 224-283, specifically `proc_references` at ~line 268). Note `signature_scan::types::ParamDef` (rust/tcl-compiler/src/signature_scan/types.rs:37) doesn't even carry a per-parameter name_span — only the separate scope-chain `VarDef` (used exclusively by the `$`-gated path) has real spans, which is why the `$destroy` case works but the bare declaration-site case has nothing to anchor a "this is my own parameter" check against.
